Quantization for llms

- More bits, more accurate  
  -  Larger data type, means models are more accurate  
  - Inference is slower  
  - Purpose is to rescale weights to reduce memory and requirements while minimizing accuracy  
- Usually is int8 and int4  
  - We need to rescale weights  
- In order to rescale, usually you need a function to remap to a lower-precision space  
  - Example rescaling float32 to int 8  
- Picking alpha and beta range,simple could be minimum and maximum which doesn’t work well if the alpha and beta are outliers, mostly because you are compressing the average closer together  
  - You could drop outliers, but if there are plenty then it may hurt accurayc  
- The optimization is how to minimize loss of accuracy whilst quantizing  
  - The calibrater to use KL divergence  
- When can we apply the technique  
  - Post-training dynamic quantization  
    - Laid the model and adjust weights  
    - Load the model, and redo it  
    - There is dynamic so its slower  
  - Post training static quantization  
    - Be mindful of accuracy if you use it on differing datasets  
  - Quantization-aware training  
    - Training with full precision, but this is the most expensive usually  
- Zero quant is the first one optimized for LLMs,   
- Partition into groups, and quantize separately  
- Token-wise quantization for activiation

![][image1]  
Weight and activations are different across layers, and ranges more so

- DPTQ for ZeroQuant, bitsandbytes is DPTQ and it more efficiently than normal types  
  - Bitsandbytes quantizes outliers separately with mixed-precision decomposition (16-bit) and works best with large models, but is otherwise slower on smaller onesddddd  
- D or SPTQ for smoothquant, migrate to the weight layers  
- GPTQ, static post-training quantization, can go down to 2 bit precision   
- AWQ, 0.1-1% of weights have critical influence, they are not quantized but the rest are

Bert high level overview notes  
\- bert is bidirection encoder representations for transformers  
	\- does things like sentiment analysis, NLP tasks like translation, I think it is the backbone for chatgpt  
\- its trained on a bunch of NLP, i.e Wikipedia, Masked language models are intentionally removing words and BERT idea is to pick up context before and after the sentence to guess the missing words, sentence prediction by predicting whether or not two sentences are related to one either "went to the store, bought cheese" versus "went to the store. A nuclear bomb was dropped in the ocean". Uses transformers to observe relationship between words  
transformers leverage self attention mechanisms, and are trained to typically figure out what is worth retaining and what isn't, using there is a encoder decoder architecture, but bert is decoder only

RAG high level overview notes

basically rag allows for information retrieval before generating response, preventing the need to retrain a llm, rag can also cit sources. still limited insofar as it may still misunderstand context, such as a title of a book being rhetorical or a joke "Pol pot, the first democratic mayor of New York"  
rag converts information into embeddings which get stored in a vector database for retrieval, the retrieval is included in the original query, new implementations can make self-improvements  
typically you gotta chunk so that info is easier to take  
some people have used the internet to try to fill in extra context where the information may not be found in the database  
doesn't prevent hallucinations  
when giving conflicting information, RAG will struggle.

The grad in this case would be the derivative  
Calculating the gradient with respect to scalars is effectively chain rule in a micrograd NN  
For manual backpropogation, all you really need is to know the derivative
